subject: Next steps: FastTxn capacity & deployment path recap

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + clarifying throughput/latency for FastTxn pilot

Hi Samantha / David —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of the main signals we captured and a few clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

What we heard:
- Primary use: real-time fraud scoring and contextual enrichment for checkout flows.
- Critical p95 latency for inference inline with checkout: target <= 100 ms for single-turn scoring.
- Expected peak traffic: baseline 200 QPS with spikes up to ~600 QPS during promos.
- Overnight batch enrichment (large, async jobs) that can be scheduled off-peak.
- Sensitive PII in some logs; compliance is a check (SOC2 and encryption at rest).

Clarifying asks (if you can confirm in a quick reply):
1) For the 600 QPS spike, what percentage is sustained vs <5-minute bursts?
2) Do you require customer-managed keys or can we use Redwood-managed KMS for the pilot?
3) Any region constraints (we heard US-east preferred)?

Initial thinking — if the p95 requirement is consistently <=100 ms and bursts to 600 QPS are short, Hosted with autoscaling and prefix caching could work and will be fastest to get started. If you need strict throughput guarantees and predictable latency under sustained 600 QPS, Dedicated reserved capacity is the safer path. Private VPC would be for stricter data residency / key control.

I attached a rough capacity estimate and our SLA options. Marissa / Diego — please add technical notes we should share with FastTxn to make the choice easier.

Next step: If you confirm the three clarifying items, we’ll send a short pilot proposal (2-week pilot with traffic replay + RPS tests) and a cost outline.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: fasttxn_capacity_estimate.xlsx, redwood_sla_options.pdf
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fasttxn.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying throughput/latency for FastTxn pilot

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the summary, that matches our internal notes. Quick answers:
1) Spikes to ~600 QPS are typically short — median burst length last quarter was ~3 minutes, but during flash sales we've seen 10-15 minute windows a few times/month. Overall sustained baseline is ~180-250 QPS.
2) For the pilot we can use Redwood-managed KMS; long-term we prefer customer-managed keys (we can discuss during procurement).
3) Yes, US-East primarily.

A couple more details that matter for the recommendation:
- We need p95 <=100 ms for the inline scoring path. If a fallback path is needed during extreme spikes, we can accept degraded scoring (e.g., simpler model returning default risk) for up to 2 minutes while the system scales.
- Batch enrichment jobs run overnight (1–3 AM) and can be throttled.
- Compliance: SOC2 documentation will be required for procurement; happy to start with the SOC2 summary you attached.

Would like to see a concrete recommendation from Redwood on whether Hosted can meet p95 100ms with autoscale + caching for our profile, and a Dedicated pricing example (monthly committed + burst).

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Product, FastTxn
Samantha.Lee@fasttxn.com

Hi Samantha / David —

Appreciate the details — below is a pragmatic recommendation and the tradeoffs. I’m Marissa from Solutions Engineering; Diego and I worked up a short playbook to validate the path during a 2-week pilot.

Short recommendation (TL;DR):
- Pilot immediately on Hosted API to validate latency profile and caching effectiveness. Hosted + continuous batching + prefix KV cache should hit p95 ~80–120 ms for the scoring model in our tests at baseline QPS.
- If your 600 QPS bursts become sustained (>10 minutes) or you require hard throughput SLAs, transition to Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) with burst pools. Dedicated will give predictable tail latency and lower cost per token at scale.
- Private VPC only if you need CMK or strict network isolation for production (procurement signal).

Why Hosted first:
- Fastest path: no infra onboarding, immediate telemetry, and we can run traffic replay from your logs.
- We’ll instrument prefix caching and recommend quantization profiles for your model to reduce per-token latency.

What we’ll validate in the 2-week pilot:
1) P95 latency at baseline (200 QPS) with live traffic and replayed spikes to 600 QPS.
2) Cost / token sensitivity with different batching windows.
3) Effectiveness of prefix/KV caching for cold-starts.
4) Failure modes and a fallback policy (simpler model + default risk path) for the 2-minute degraded period you mentioned.

Deliverables and artifacts we’ll provide:
- Pilot runbook and test schedule (attached in Drive link).
- Capacity and estimated pricing for Dedicated if needed (attached: fasttxn_capacity_estimate.xlsx).
- SOC2 summary and our standard security checklist (attached: soc2_summary.pdf).

Practical notes for the pilot:
- We’ll need a 2–3 hour window with your infra/engineers to set up traffic replay and a small API key for the sandbox.
- If you want CMK for the pilot, we can do a gated test in Private VPC but that will add 2–3 weeks for provisioning.

Rishi / Diego — I’ll prepare a one-page pilot proposal and pricing scenarios (Hosted pilot estimate + Dedicated commit tiers with burst) by Friday. Samantha / David — does next Tuesday morning work for the 2–3 hour replay setup?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
